occupations.name: Spring Keeper
occupations.description: Protects a shared spring from contamination, allocates access, and maintains channels and basins.

occupations.name: Charcoal Burner
occupations.description: Builds and tends covered charcoal clamps, balancing fuel quality against sustainable cutting.

occupations.name: Beekeeper
occupations.description: Maintains skeps, manages swarms, and harvests honey and wax without exhausting colonies needed for winter.

occupations.name: Shipwright
occupations.description: Builds and repairs clinker-built boats, shaping frames and overlapping planks by hand.

occupations.name: Causeway Keeper
occupations.description: Maintains raised paths, brush foundations, markers, and emergency shelter across wet ground.

occupations.name: Harbor Master
occupations.description: Allocates berths, records harbor dues, organizes pilots, and keeps channels and quay rules known.

occupations.name: Quarry Master
occupations.description: Plans safe extraction, controls wedges and lifting work, grades stone, and accounts for deliveries.

occupations.name: Timber Hewyer
occupations.description: Splits trunks along the grain with wedges, squares beams with a broad axe, and dresses boards with axes, adzes, and planes.

occupations.name: Weir Keeper
occupations.description: Operates removable weir gates and hauling ways, schedules passage, records tolls, watches water levels, and organizes maintenance labor.

occupations.name: Fisher
occupations.description: Works local waters with nets, lines, traps, and seasonal knowledge, then preserves or sells the catch.

occupations.name: Shrine Keeper
occupations.description: Maintains a local shrine, organizes practical rites, receives modest offerings, and keeps the place available to the community.

occupations.name: Weaver
occupations.description: Turns spun wool or flax into cloth and judges sett, tension, finishing, and repair.

occupations.name: Cooper
occupations.description: Makes and repairs staved tubs, buckets, churns, casks, and fish barrels.

occupations.name: Mine Overseer
occupations.description: Assigns crews, records who is underground, monitors timbering and drainage, and accounts for ore raised.

occupations.name: Tar Burner
occupations.description: Produces pine tar in slow earthen kilns and prepares pitch for boats, roofs, rope, and timber.

occupations.name: Lawman
occupations.description: Recites customary law, prepares cases for the thing, and helps witnesses state oaths and settlements precisely.

occupations.name: Miller
occupations.description: Operates and maintains a watermill, measures grain, and takes an agreed portion as the milling fee.

occupations.name: Ritual Speaker
occupations.description: Leads witnessed oaths, seasonal recitations, and public remembrance without belonging to a centralized priesthood.

occupations.name: Farmer
occupations.description: Manages fields, livestock, manure, seed, hay, and the household labor calendar.

occupations.name: Herbalist
occupations.description: Gathers, dries, and prepares familiar medicinal plants while distinguishing useful remedies from dangerous claims.

occupations.name: Ferryman
occupations.description: Carries people, animals, and goods across a regular ferry reach and judges when current or weather makes passage unsafe.

occupations.name: Tanner
occupations.description: Cures hides with bark, fat, smoke, and careful washing for shoes, harness, bags, and clothing.

occupations.name: Hunter
occupations.description: Tracks game, observes seasonal limits, supplies meat and hides, and guides others through wooded country.

occupations.name: Horse Breeder
occupations.description: Breeds, trains, and trades working horses suited to local roads, fields, and winter fodder limits.

occupations.name: Guide
occupations.description: Leads travelers through locally difficult ground and is responsible for honest warnings about weather and route conditions.

occupations.name: Blacksmith
occupations.description: Forges and repairs agricultural tools, fittings, nails, weapons, and household ironwork.

occupations.name: Potter
occupations.description: Shapes and fires household vessels, storage jars, lamps, and coarse industrial ware.

occupations.name: Innkeeper
occupations.description: Keeps lodging, food, drink, stabling, accounts, and household order at an inn or guesthouse.

occupations.name: Pass Keeper
occupations.description: Maintains a mountain shelter and route markers, reports hazards, and guides travelers when conditions permit.

occupations.name: Brewer
occupations.description: Malts grain, manages fermentation, and supplies ale for households, inns, feasts, and labor crews.

occupations.name: Wheelwright
occupations.description: Builds wheels, axles, carts, and sled fittings suited to local roads and loads.

civilization_races.description: Humans make up Tyrven's known communities; regional identity is cultural, legal, linguistic, and economic rather than biological.

races.name: Human
races.description: The people of Audrun are human. Regional differences in language, custom, diet, and appearance reflect ancestry and environment.

character_roles.name: Ritual Speaker
character_roles.description: Conducts public rites and frames spoken obligations while remaining dependent on community recognition rather than supernatural authority.

character_roles.name: Causeway Keeper
character_roles.description: Inspects raised roads through wet ground, calls agreed repair labor, marks closures, and keeps brush, stakes, and stone ready for flood damage.

character_roles.name: Shipwright
character_roles.description: Designs, builds, repairs, and launches clinker-built vessels while coordinating timber, iron fittings, rope, sail work, and skilled yard labor.

character_roles.name: Beekeeper
character_roles.description: Maintains skeps, manages swarms, harvests honey and wax, and negotiates seasonal access to meadow and woodland forage.

character_roles.name: Harbor Master
character_roles.description: Assigns berths, maintains movement and safety rules, records harbor dues, and mediates between fishers, merchants, and public obligations.

character_roles.name: First Housecarl
character_roles.description: Commander of the sovereign’s personal guard.

character_roles.name: Silver Warden
character_roles.description: Keeper of mint standards, coin weights, and silver purity.

character_roles.name: Lawman
character_roles.description: Recites and interprets district custom, orders hearings, records settlements through witnesses, and identifies cases requiring higher judgment.

character_roles.name: Royal Steward
character_roles.description: Steward of the royal household, traveling provisions, and central accounts; not an independent regent.

character_roles.name: Horse Breeder
character_roles.description: Manages breeding, fodder, training, and exchange of horses suited to local terrain, farm work, transport, and mounted service.

character_roles.name: Sawyer
character_roles.description: Selects and seasons timber, operates sawpits with a partner crew, grades boards, and maintains cutting and ownership marks.

character_roles.name: Fisher
character_roles.description: Works local waters under customary seasons, mesh rules, spawning closures, and household claims.

character_roles.name: High King
character_roles.description: Sovereign and war leader confirmed by the Great Thing.

character_roles.name: Innkeeper
character_roles.description: Runs lodging, food, drink, stabling, witnessed exchange, and local information at a settlement or road house.

character_roles.name: Lawspeaker
character_roles.description: Independent custodian and interpreter of Tyrven law.

character_roles.name: Miller
character_roles.description: Operates and repairs a watermill, keeps public measures, schedules limited water, and accounts for grain received and meal returned.

character_roles.name: Jarl
character_roles.description: A provincial ruler responsible for law, taxation, defense, and negotiation with local assemblies and the crown.

character_roles.name: Quarry Master
character_roles.description: Reads fracture and weathering, directs safe extraction and dressing, and accounts for stone, labor, waste, and transport.

character_roles.name: Ferryman
character_roles.description: Carries people, animals, messages, and goods across water while judging current, wind, ice, load, and landing safety.

character_roles.name: Tar Burner
character_roles.description: Extracts tar and pitch from controlled pine material, maintains fire safety, and prepares waterproofing for hulls, roofs, rope, and exposed wood.

character_roles.name: Pass Keeper
character_roles.description: Maintains markers and shelters, reports conditions, organizes rescue, and closes a high route when travel becomes unreasonably dangerous.

character_roles.name: Weir Keeper
character_roles.description: Coordinates passage through a flash weir, water release, hauling labor, warning signals, repairs, and toll tallies.

character_roles.name: Charcoal Burner
character_roles.description: Cuts wood under local rotation rules and manages slow earth-covered burns that supply smithies and smelting hearths.

character_roles.name: Herbalist
character_roles.description: Collects, prepares, and trades useful plants while distinguishing practical remedies from uncertain or harmful claims.

character_roles.name: Speaker of Jarls
character_roles.description: A jarl chosen by the provincial rulers to present their common position at the Great Thing; the mandate lasts only while their confidence holds.

character_roles.name: Succession Claimant
character_roles.description: An acknowledged adult of a ruling lineage who may present a claim when a provincial jarldom becomes vacant.

character_roles.name: Mine Overseer
character_roles.description: Coordinates mine crews, drainage, timbering, ore sorting, safety closure, and witnessed division of output.

character_roles.name: Guide
character_roles.description: Leads travelers through dangerous or poorly marked country using local knowledge of weather, water, paths, shelter, and seasonal hazards.

character_roles.name: Hunter
character_roles.description: Provides meat, hides, and field knowledge under local rules governing seasons, breeding grounds, traps, and access.

character_roles.name: Spring Keeper
character_roles.description: Maintains common access and cleanliness at a spring, regulates channels and washing places, and reports contamination or failing flow.

character_roles.name: Shrine Keeper
character_roles.description: Maintains a local sacred place, receives and accounts for offerings, preserves its customary rites, and organizes associated practical obligations.

character_roles.name: Stallari
character_roles.description: Marshal of the royal household, hird, and wartime levy.

character_roles.name: Blacksmith
character_roles.description: Works bloomery iron into tools, fittings, weapons, and repairs while judging material quality and rationing scarce charcoal.

tax_policies.name: Eirsund Weir and Channel Due
tax_policies.description: One penning is due from each laden freight barge passing the Great Flash Weir. Empty return craft, local fishing boats, rescue traffic, and boats carrying labor or materials for waterway repair pass without charge. The weir keeper records passage publicly, and most receipts remain in Eirholm for gates, hauling ways, towpaths, banks, markers, and bridges. Receipts assigned to an office remain public funds recorded before the appropriate thing and may be spent only on the stated service.
tax_policies.commodity: laden freight barge passing the Great Flash Weir

assessments.description: Ordinary-year assessment for year 418, recording the eligible base, observed coverage, cash, goods, and customary labor without treating office shares as personal income.
assessments.assessed_unit: laden freight barge passing the Great Flash Weir
assessments.valuation_basis: The count records eligible units observed or apportioned during year 418. Cash, goods, and labor are kept separately and converted only for the public assessment total.

exemptions.name: Eirwater Passage Weir-Labor Credit
exemptions.description: Halves the weir due for registered passage barges whose crews provide scheduled labor on towpaths, banks, markers, removable gates, and hauling ways. Fractions of a penning are accumulated in the route account and settled over several passages.

tax_policies.name: Vardborg Bridge Toll
tax_policies.description: One penning is charged per laden commercial wagon crossing the Great Bridge. People on foot, led animals, local farm carts traveling to the thing, emergency grain, and levy movement are free of toll. Rates and collections are posted at the Bridge Inn, and the provincial thing may inspect the account. Receipts assigned to an office remain public funds recorded before the appropriate thing and may be spent only on the stated service.
tax_policies.commodity: laden commercial wagon crossing the Great Bridge

assessments.description: Ordinary-year assessment for year 418, recording the eligible base, observed coverage, cash, goods, and customary labor without treating office shares as personal income.
assessments.assessed_unit: laden commercial wagon crossing the Great Bridge
assessments.valuation_basis: The count records eligible units observed or apportioned during year 418. Cash, goods, and labor are kept separately and converted only for the public assessment total.

tax_policies.name: Common Leidang Obligation
tax_policies.description: A collective defense obligation confirmed by the Great Thing. Coastal districts provide ships, crew, rigging, and provisions; inland districts provide wagons, horses, food, or equivalent labor. Eighteen pennings per assessed crew-bench is the public commutation rate when an accepted shortage must be made good in silver. It cannot be demanded for an overseas war without separate assent. Receipts assigned to an office remain public funds recorded before the appropriate thing and may be spent only on the stated service.

assessments.description: Ordinary-year assessment for year 418, recording the eligible base, observed coverage, cash, goods, and customary labor without treating office shares as personal income.
assessments.valuation_basis: The count records eligible units observed or apportioned during year 418. Cash, goods, and labor are kept separately and converted only for the public assessment total.

tax_policies.name: Royal Guesting Due
tax_policies.description: An annual obligation supporting lawful royal travel, messengers, and the limited household of the High King. It is normally rendered as grain, butter, dried fish, ale, fodder, or lodging according to local production; six pennings is the conversion value when delivery in kind is impractical. Poor households and those already providing equivalent service are not assessed, and increases require the Great Thing. Receipts assigned to an office remain public funds recorded before the appropriate thing and may be spent only on the stated service.

assessments.description: Ordinary-year assessment for year 418, recording the eligible base, observed coverage, cash, goods, and customary labor without treating office shares as personal income.
assessments.valuation_basis: The count records eligible units observed or apportioned during year 418. Cash, goods, and labor are kept separately and converted only for the public assessment total.

exemptions.name: Frostgard Winter-Capacity Allowance
exemptions.description: Reduces Frostgard's assessed royal guesting obligation by forty percent because of its short growing season, costly winter transport, and existing frontier shelter and patrol duties. The remaining obligation is assessed collectively and is usually rendered in preserved fish, hides, fodder, or lodging.

exemptions.name: Brannskar Provision Allowance
exemptions.description: Reduces Brannskar's guesting obligation by twenty-five percent because its thin volcanic soils and limited grazing cannot reliably provision a traveling court despite the value of its stone and mineral trade. The province still owes lodging, transport, and locally available stores.

tax_policies.name: Kaldhavn Harbor Due
tax_policies.description: Two pennings are due when a laden merchant vessel enters the protected inner harbor. Local fishing craft, rescue boats, royal-defense vessels on lawful service, and ships forced in solely by dangerous weather do not pay. Receipts support quays, beacons, dredging, rescue rope, and storm repairs. Receipts assigned to an office remain public funds recorded before the appropriate thing and may be spent only on the stated service.
tax_policies.commodity: laden merchant vessel entering the inner harbor

assessments.description: Ordinary-year assessment for year 418, recording the eligible base, observed coverage, cash, goods, and customary labor without treating office shares as personal income.
assessments.assessed_unit: laden merchant vessel entering the inner harbor
assessments.valuation_basis: The count records eligible units observed or apportioned during year 418. Cash, goods, and labor are kept separately and converted only for the public assessment total.

exemptions.name: Western Sea Lane Beacon-and-Rescue Credit
exemptions.description: Halves the harbor due for registered traffic on the Western Sea Lane. In return, its regular carriers maintain minor beacons, report shoaling and storm damage, carry urgent notices, and assist vessels in distress when they can do so safely.

tax_policies.name: Jarnfell Chartered Iron Due
tax_policies.description: Six percent of the recorded value of saleable iron leaving chartered workings is due after ore sorting and necessary mine costs, not from workers' wages. The provincial share maintains drainage, gallery timber, retaining walls, and protected pass roads; the crown share reflects defense demand for iron and enforcement of charter rights. Receipts assigned to an office remain public funds recorded before the appropriate thing and may be spent only on the stated service.
tax_policies.commodity: saleable ore, blooms, and bar iron from chartered workings

assessments.description: Ordinary-year assessment for year 418, recording the eligible base, observed coverage, cash, goods, and customary labor without treating office shares as personal income.
assessments.valuation_basis: Taxable goods are grouped into witnessed value bands using public weights and seasonal market prices; the percentage is the accounting equivalent of those bands.

tax_policies.name: Myrholt Causeway Toll
tax_policies.description: One penning is due from a laden commercial cart using the maintained fen causeways. Residents performing their assigned repair labor, people on foot, local fishing boats passing beneath bridges, and evacuation traffic during floods are exempt by custom. Revenue is reserved chiefly for brush foundations, dikes, gates, bridges, and shelter stores. Receipts assigned to an office remain public funds recorded before the appropriate thing and may be spent only on the stated service.
tax_policies.commodity: laden commercial cart using a maintained fen causeway

assessments.description: Ordinary-year assessment for year 418, recording the eligible base, observed coverage, cash, goods, and customary labor without treating office shares as personal income.
assessments.assessed_unit: laden commercial cart using a maintained fen causeway
assessments.valuation_basis: The count records eligible units observed or apportioned during year 418. Cash, goods, and labor are kept separately and converted only for the public assessment total.

tax_policies.name: Solmark Grain-Market Due
tax_policies.description: Two percent of witnessed bulk grain sales at chartered markets is collected in grain or its posted silver equivalent. Seed grain, household milling, rents paid directly in produce, and relief grain are outside the assessment. The retained share maintains public scales, canals, sluices, mill races, and field drains. Receipts assigned to an office remain public funds recorded before the appropriate thing and may be spent only on the stated service.
tax_policies.commodity: bulk grain sold at chartered markets

assessments.description: Ordinary-year assessment for year 418, recording the eligible base, observed coverage, cash, goods, and customary labor without treating office shares as personal income.
assessments.valuation_basis: Taxable goods are grouped into witnessed value bands using public weights and seasonal market prices; the percentage is the accounting equivalent of those bands.

tax_policies.name: Ravnskog Marked-Timber Duty
tax_policies.description: Four percent of the witnessed export value of marked timber, tar, resin, and pitch is due before the goods leave the province. Household fuel, farm repairs, customary gathering, and timber assigned to bridge or firebreak work are not taxed. The retained share supports boundary inspection, sustainable cutting, firebreaks, roads, and river landings. Receipts assigned to an office remain public funds recorded before the appropriate thing and may be spent only on the stated service.
tax_policies.commodity: commercial timber, tar, resin, and pitch bearing district marks

assessments.description: Ordinary-year assessment for year 418, recording the eligible base, observed coverage, cash, goods, and customary labor without treating office shares as personal income.
assessments.valuation_basis: Taxable goods are grouped into witnessed value bands using public weights and seasonal market prices; the percentage is the accounting equivalent of those bands.

exemptions.name: Raven Timber Run Mark-and-Patrol Credit
exemptions.description: Reduces the marked-timber duty by one quarter for goods using the Raven Timber Run. Route households maintain timber marks, river landings, firebreaks, and boundary patrols, lowering the province's collection and enforcement costs.

tax_policies.name: Brannskar Dressed-Stone Duty
tax_policies.description: Four percent of the recorded sale value of dressed stone exported from Brannskar is due at the loading yard. Rough stone gathered for household building and stone supplied for public road repair are not assessed. Receipts fund quarry inspection, lifting gear, retaining walls, slope clearance, and roads to the quays. Receipts assigned to an office remain public funds recorded before the appropriate thing and may be spent only on the stated service.
tax_policies.commodity: dressed basalt, paving stone, and millstones

assessments.description: Ordinary-year assessment for year 418, recording the eligible base, observed coverage, cash, goods, and customary labor without treating office shares as personal income.
assessments.valuation_basis: Taxable goods are grouped into witnessed value bands using public weights and seasonal market prices; the percentage is the accounting equivalent of those bands.

exemptions.name: Ashen Road Maintenance Credit
exemptions.description: Reduces the dressed-stone export duty by one quarter for loads using the Ashen Road because its chartered carriers provide retaining-wall, drainage, slope-clearance, and shelter labor on the difficult upland route.

tax_policies.name: Frostgard Fur-Market Fee
tax_policies.description: A fee of two and one-half percent on witnessed commercial sales at recognized fur markets. Household use, gifts, compensation payments, and small direct barter are outside the assessment. Most proceeds maintain winter roads, market weights, patrol shelters, and emergency stores. Receipts assigned to an office remain public funds recorded before the appropriate thing and may be spent only on the stated service.
tax_policies.commodity: commercial sales of pelts, hides, and finished winter clothing

gods.domain: oaths, law, guest-right, and the peace of assemblies
gods.description: Haldren presides over sworn law, public witness, and judgments spoken before the thing.
gods.pantheon: The Seven recognized at the Great Thing

gods.name: Morna
gods.domain: the dead, ancestral memory, burial, and winter
gods.description: Morna is invoked at burial mounds and family graves, where households keep names, inheritance, and obligations to the dead.
gods.pantheon: The Seven recognized at the Great Thing

gods.name: Keldra
gods.domain: stone, springs, iron, quarrying, and skilled craft
gods.description: Keldra is honored where useful stone, clean water, or workable ore emerges from the ground. Smiths, miners, quarry workers, and spring keepers leave small portions of charcoal, grain, or shaped scrap as thanks for materials used without waste.
gods.pantheon: The Seven recognized at the Great Thing

gods.name: Veyr
gods.domain: fields, grazing, seasonal rain, and harvest
gods.description: Veyr is associated with worked soil, healthy pasture, and the uncertain balance between rain and clear weather. Farmers mark the first furrow and the final sheaf in his name, but good husbandry is considered the proper form of devotion.
gods.pantheon: The Seven recognized at the Great Thing

gods.name: Saeva
gods.domain: sea, tides, wind, fishing, and safe return
gods.description: Saeva guards coastal households, fishers, safe landfall, and the customary sharing of a catch after a dangerous voyage.
gods.pantheon: The Seven recognized at the Great Thing

gods.name: Eldra
gods.domain: hearth, kinship, birth, hospitality, and household stores
gods.description: Eldra is honored at the central fire and at communal ovens. Her customs concern care within the household, fair division of stored food, protection of children, and the obligations owed to kin, fosterlings, servants, and guests.
gods.pantheon: The Seven recognized at the Great Thing

gods.name: Skarven
gods.domain: roads, boundaries, trade, ferries, and travelers
gods.description: Skarven watches over negotiated passage: roads kept open, ferries fairly priced, boundaries clearly witnessed, and strangers given reliable directions. His roadside shrines are simple cairns repaired by those who use the route.
gods.pantheon: The Seven recognized at the Great Thing

continents.name: Tyrven
continents.description: Tyrven is a deeply indented northern continent of western fjords, central river basins, eastern mountains and forests, southern farming plains, and subarctic northern highlands. Nine provinces share assemblies, customary law, coastal routes, and an inland network of rivers and roads. Vardborg is the royal seat, while provincial jarls maintain strong local estates and followings.

currency.name: Tyrven Pennings
currency.description: Tyrven Pennings are small silver coins and a public unit of account, stamped with a longship prow and an angular knotwork seal. Coin is common at major markets and in official payments, but larger transactions also use foreign coins, ingots, arm rings, and cut silver accepted by tested weight and purity. Local dues may be rendered in goods or labor at witnessed conversion rates.

calendars.name: Tyrven Reckoning
calendars.description: Tyrven Reckoning divides the ordinary year into twelve named months totaling 364 days. Seven public feast days follow the final winter month every seventh year, giving a long-term mean of 365 days.
calendars.intercalation_rule: Seven intercalary feast days follow the final winter month every seventh year. Courts suspend ordinary hearings while households settle accounts and renew public oaths.

provinces.climate_zone: Subarctic along the fjords and polar on the highest plateaus.
provinces.moisture_regime: Low precipitation inland, with heavier snow on the western slopes and fjord coast.
provinces.elevation_profile: Glaciated plateaus rise into steep peaks, with narrow habitable valleys descending to deep fjords.

continents.major_watersheds: Short western rivers descend through fjords, the Varda system gathers central and eastern mountain water before turning south, Myrholt and Eirholm occupy low lake basins, and colder eastern rivers reach the northeastern sea.
continents.ocean_currents: A warm northeast-flowing current moderates the western coast and keeps many outer fjords seasonally open, while cold polar water descends along the northeastern shelf.
continents.prevailing_winds: Moist westerlies bring heavy precipitation to the western coasts and mountains, leaving parts of the interior in a rain shadow. Polar easterlies affect the far north most strongly in winter.
continents.tectonic_setting: A stable cratonic interior lies between ancient folded mountain belts in the west and east. The deeply glaciated western margin is now tectonically quiet, while the southwest preserves an old basalt province formed by extinct rifting or hotspot activity and cut by residual spring-bearing faults.

water_bodies.name: Skeld Sea
water_bodies.description: The broad western sea serves the harbors of Skeldvik and the black-rock coast of Brannskar.

province_links.description: The western province faces the island-strewn inner sea.
The western edge of Solmark reaches the sea below the coastal road.
Basalt cliffs and small coves line the southwestern shore.

water_bodies.prevailing_conditions: Westerly swells strengthen after the autumn equinox; summer mornings are often fogbound.
water_bodies.hazards: Skerries, lee-shore surf, and sudden squalls around the outer islands.

water_bodies.name: Sivvatn
water_bodies.description: A shallow reed lake whose islands support fishing camps, grazing, and small farmsteads above flood level.

province_links.description: Siv Lake occupies the reed-island country around Sivholm.

water_bodies.prevailing_conditions: Spring floods spread among the reed islands; summer leaves sheltered channels between firm banks.
water_bodies.hazards: Flooded reeds, soft banks, insects, and channels that shift after high water.

water_bodies.name: Vikvatn
water_bodies.description: A fish-rich lake beside Vatnvik, with sheltered beaches, reed margins, and a small seasonal camp.

province_links.description: Vatnvik Lake occupies a sheltered basin above the main channel.

water_bodies.prevailing_conditions: Sheltered water drains through a short navigable channel into the Eirholm network.
water_bodies.hazards: Soft reed banks, winter ice, and low late-summer levels.

water_bodies.name: Eirwater
water_bodies.description: A navigable river and channel network linking Eirholm’s lakes with Vardalen and the southern basin.

province_links.description: Wetland rivers feed the southern Eirwater basin.
Managed southern channels join the lower river.
Lakes, channels, and towpaths form the navigable middle reach.
Eastern mountain streams supply the upper basin.
The main channel crosses the central valley below Vardborg.

water_bodies.prevailing_conditions: Spring snowmelt raises the current; summer levels favor barges and towpaths.
water_bodies.hazards: Flash weirs, bridge piers, submerged timber, and winter ice.

water_bodies.name: Steinvik
water_bodies.description: A deep glacial inlet with a natural harbor, working quarries, and shore yards for fishing and cargo vessels.

province_links.description: Stone Bay cuts into the working coast at Steinvik.

water_bodies.prevailing_conditions: The narrow inlet is sheltered from western swell but funnels hard squalls from the stone valley.
water_bodies.hazards: Submerged rock shelves, gusting crosswinds, and a narrow outer approach.

water_bodies.name: Vesthavnsund
water_bodies.description: The outer sound leading to Vesthavn’s quay and the western coastal road.

province_links.description: The sound forms Vesthavn’s outer harbor approach.

water_bodies.prevailing_conditions: Ocean swell weakens inside the outer headlands, leaving a dependable harbor approach.
water_bodies.hazards: Cross-currents at the mouth and fog against the western cliffs.

water_bodies.name: Solmark Gulf
water_bodies.description: The sheltered southern gulf receives Tyrven’s principal river and serves the grain ports of Solmark.

province_links.description: Grain ports and sheltered roadsteads line the gulf.
The southern basalt coast closes the western side of the gulf.

water_bodies.prevailing_conditions: Mild southerly water, regular tides, and afternoon sea breezes reach far into the gulf.
water_bodies.hazards: Autumn storm surges, shifting bars, and crowded approaches during harvest shipping.

water_bodies.name: Hrafnsfjord
water_bodies.description: A deep glacial inlet serving Hrafnsfjord and the northern fishing grounds.

province_links.description: The fjord cuts deep into the northern highlands.

water_bodies.prevailing_conditions: Deep water and steep walls shelter the inner quay from ocean swell.
water_bodies.hazards: Falling stone, downslope gusts, and shore ice at the head of the inlet.

water_bodies.name: Ravna
water_bodies.description: A fast timber river descending from Ravnskog toward the western sea.

province_links.description: The timber river descends through the western forest.
The Ravna reaches the sea through Skeldvik’s coastal ridge.

water_bodies.prevailing_conditions: Snowmelt carries timber swiftly west; summer flow is steadier but shallower.
water_bodies.hazards: Log jams, rock ledges, and rapid water below the forest landings.

water_bodies.name: Varda Estuary
water_bodies.description: The lower Varda broadens into a working estuary above the Solmark Gulf.

province_links.description: Reed banks and tidal channels occupy the lower plain.
The Varda carries the central basin toward tidewater.

water_bodies.prevailing_conditions: The tide reaches inland through broad reed margins and silt channels.
water_bodies.hazards: Moving sandbars, tidal bores after storms, and dense morning fog.

water_bodies.name: Svanesund
water_bodies.description: A narrow island passage on the Skeldvik coast, favored by pilots in settled weather.

province_links.description: The sound passes among Skeldvik’s low western islands.

water_bodies.prevailing_conditions: Tides run briskly between low islands and sheltered anchorages.
water_bodies.hazards: Skerries, tidal races, and fog close to the water.

water_bodies.name: Ulf Sea
water_bodies.description: The remote northeastern sea borders Frostgard and the forested headlands beyond Ravnskog.

province_links.description: Remote northeastern headlands face the Ulf Sea.
Forested eastern headlands reach the southern edge of the Ulf Sea.

water_bodies.prevailing_conditions: Cold easterly water and long winter darkness keep the northern coast cool through spring.
water_bodies.hazards: Pack ice, fog banks, and few dependable anchorages.

water_bodies.name: Langvatn
water_bodies.description: The largest of Eirholm’s long lakes, used by fishers, ferries, and shallow cargo boats.

province_links.description: Long Lake lies within the eastern lake country.

water_bodies.prevailing_conditions: Calm summer water gives way to early mist and dependable winter ice.
water_bodies.hazards: Reed shallows, sudden lake squalls, and weak ice near the outlet.

water_bodies.name: Hrim River
water_bodies.description: The forest river drains Icewater Lake and carries timber and small boats toward the northern coast.

province_links.description: The Hrim drains the forested interior toward the northern coast.

water_bodies.prevailing_conditions: Snowmelt carries a strong early current; summer water is lower and easier to ford.
water_bodies.hazards: Timber jams, cold rapids, and shifting gravel bars below the forest reaches.

water_bodies.name: Hrafn Sea
water_bodies.description: The northern sea lies beyond the Frostgard fjords. Cold northern water dominates the outer basin, while a narrower western branch carries milder water toward Hrafnsfjord during much of the year.

province_links.description: Northern fjords open onto the cold Hrafn Sea.
The outer northern islands mark the turn into the Hrafn Sea.

water_bodies.prevailing_conditions: Cold northern currents meet open-ocean weather along a steep, broken coast.
water_bodies.hazards: Winter gales, drift ice near shore, and violent cross-seas off the headlands.

water_bodies.name: Ulf Shelf
water_bodies.description: A shallow shelf of banks and fishing grounds along the inner margin of the Ulf Sea.

province_links.description: Shallow northern banks support seasonal fishing.

water_bodies.prevailing_conditions: Shallow water cools quickly in autumn and breaks into drifting ice late in spring.
water_bodies.hazards: Uncharted shoals, grounded ice, and poor visibility.

water_bodies.name: Isvatn
water_bodies.description: A high freshwater lake bordered by meadow, birch scrub, and a short summer fishing season.

province_links.description: Icewater Lake lies in the high Isdal basin.

water_bodies.prevailing_conditions: The lake remains icebound through much of winter and rises sharply during the spring thaw.
water_bodies.hazards: Late ice, cold water, and sudden wind descending from the Isdal slopes.

guilds.name: Kaldhavn Shipwright Fellowship
guilds.description: Independent shipwright households meet here to inspect timber, organize launch crews, train apprentices, aid injured yard workers, and negotiate royal requisitions.
guilds.alignment: practical, independent, and protective of skilled labor

guilds.name: Myrholt Causeway Fellowship
guilds.description: A labor fellowship of causeway keepers, fishers, peat households, and herb gatherers. It organizes flood watches, brush and stake stores, shelter repair, and relief for communities temporarily cut off by water.
guilds.alignment: communal, flood-conscious, and protective of wetland access

guilds.name: River Millers Fellowship
guilds.description: A loose interprovincial fellowship that compares measures, shares millstone and wheel repairs, trains millers, and presents water disputes before local things. Each mill remains answerable to its own district.
guilds.alignment: standards-minded, practical, and opposed to hidden deductions

guilds.name: Jarnfell Iron Fellowship
guilds.description: A working fellowship joining mine overseers, charcoal burners, smelters, and smiths. It arbitrates material grades, injury support, apprentice obligations, and the division of scarce charcoal while resisting unsafe production demands.
guilds.alignment: craft-centered, disciplined, and skeptical of distant quotas

guilds.name: Ravnskog Timber-Mark Fellowship
guilds.description: Sawyers and raft crews use this fellowship to register cutting marks and river landings, settle lost-log claims, maintain firebreaks, and provide mutual aid.
guilds.leader: Council meeting at the Timber Inn

guilds.name: Eirwater Boat Fellowship
guilds.description: A mutual-aid association of barge households, ferrymen, pilots, and towpath crews. Members coordinate rescue, report hazards, pool replacement rope, and provide the labor that earns route toll credits. Its council is chosen seasonally at the Eirholm Thing.

guilds.name: Skeldvik Mariners Relief Fellowship
guilds.description: A coastal mutual-aid fellowship supporting search crews, bereaved boat households, fog bells, rescue rope, and reliable hazard reports. It is funded through gifts, member shares, and a small portion of harbor receipts.
guilds.alignment: mutualist, sober, and committed to rescue before ceremony

civilizations.name: Tyrven Communities
civilizations.description: The Tyrven communities belong to an early high-medieval society whose older assembly law, elective crown, provincial jarldoms, clinker-built fleets, household cults, and silver-weight customs remain in active use. Public writing, chartered mines, permanent markets, measured tolls, and maintained trunk routes have expanded since the Compact. Provincial law permits any recognized adult of a ruling lineage to present a succession claim, although wealth, kin support, estate management, and the assent of the thing determine whether that claim succeeds. Tyrven writing uses an unaccented common spelling while preserving compounds inherited from several regional dialects.
