characters.name: Svala Eiriksdottir
characters.description: Quiet and patient, Svala builds agreement by remembering household claims and old water boundaries. She seldom raises her voice, but she does not abandon a position once the evidence supports it.
characters.title: Jarl of Myrholt
characters.politics: Protects wetland commons, regulates causeway tolls, and opposes drainage schemes that would enrich a few estates at the expense of fishing villages.

characters.name: Ingrid Ragnarsdottir
characters.description: Formal and meticulous, Ingrid reads accounts before meetings and rarely improvises. She values predictable rules and judges officials by whether ordinary markets keep working.
characters.title: Jarl of Vardalen
characters.politics: Supports the crown on grain policy and road taxation while protecting the bargaining power of valley towns and large farms.

characters.name: Kari Sigvatsdottir
characters.description: Kari is sociable, skeptical, and unusually good at separating rumor from testimony.
characters.title: Keeper of the Bridge Inn

occupations.description: Keeps the principal inn beside Vardborg bridge and hosts merchants waiting on legal disputes.

characters.politics: Supports uniform bridge tolls and keeps written witness accounts when guards or collectors are accused of taking more than the posted rate.

characters.name: Sten Hakonsson
characters.description: Sten is taciturn, dependable, and exact about grain direction. He teaches by demonstrating once and then watching closely.
characters.title: Sawyer of Furudal

occupations.description: Leads the main boarding crew serving Furudal's timber trade.

characters.politics: Backs woodland rotation and wants sawpit fees used to repair the timber landing rather than absorbed into general dues.

characters.name: Kjell Arnsson
characters.description: Kjell is friendly on shore and wholly serious on the water. Passengers, animals, and cargo are loaded only when he judges the crossing safe.
characters.title: Ferryman of Nesby

occupations.description: Operates the regular ferry under rates agreed at the local thing.

characters.politics: Opposes fixed crossing quotas during flood season and insists the ferryman retain authority to stop service when the current turns dangerous.

characters.name: Finn Torkelsson
characters.description: Finn is stubborn, reliable, and happiest with a practical problem. Fresh stakes and brush markers show where he has judged the ground unsafe.
characters.title: Keeper of the North Causeway

occupations.description: Maintains the northern raised road and shelter through the wettest part of Torvmark.

characters.politics: Presses landholders on both sides of the fen to supply equal labor even when flood damage falls mostly on one stretch.

characters.name: Solveig Torbjornsdottir
characters.description: Solveig is precise, strategically patient, and unwilling to let powerful speakers replace facts with volume. She keeps careful private mnemonics but recites the law in public from memory.
characters.title: Law Reciter of Eikvang

occupations.description: Prepares cases and recites local law at the Eikvang thing under the provincial lawspeaker's oversight.

characters.politics: Defends the thing's authority over local inheritance, boundary, and compensation disputes while accepting royal judgment in matters crossing provinces.

characters.name: Torleif Eiriksson
characters.description: Torleif listens longer than most claimants and is slow to forgive anyone who shifts flood risk onto poorer households.
characters.title: Recognized kin of the Myrholt jarl
characters.politics: Defend common reed beds, drainage work, and access across the fen causeways.

characters.name: Signe Ormsdottir
characters.description: Signe is lively, shrewd, and direct about boundaries. She enjoys stories but verifies commercial claims before repeating them.
characters.title: Keeper of the Timber Inn

occupations.description: Keeps the inn used by timber buyers, raft crews, and forest households.

characters.politics: Supports common inspection of timber marks and refuses service to crews caught floating unmarked stolen logs.

characters.name: Hervor Oskdottir
characters.description: Hervor is practical, sharp-tongued, and fair. She has little patience for status once boots are muddy and beds are scarce.
characters.title: Keeper of the Spring Inn

occupations.description: Runs the town inn near the warm springs for traders, quarry crews, and visiting bathers.

characters.politics: Supports public control of spring access and refuses private rooms to anyone trying to bypass the posted bathing order.

characters.name: Ivar Knutsson
characters.description: Ivar spends much of the year among grazing households and is respected for remembering obligations that richer visitors overlook.
characters.title: Recognized kin of the Frostgard jarl
characters.politics: Keep winter stores and grazing agreements ahead of prestige building or distant war.

characters.name: Sigrid Arnesdottir
characters.description: Sigrid is exacting with ore tallies and skeptical of promises unsupported by timber, labor, or tested metal.
characters.title: Recognized kin of the Jarnfell jarl
characters.politics: Bind mine charters to drainage, road repair, and compensation for injured workers.

characters.name: Una Halldorsdottir
characters.description: Una is generous, practical, and slow to take offense. She is skilled at finding quiet compromises that still leave responsibilities clear.
characters.title: Keeper of the Bridge Inn

occupations.description: Runs the bridge inn and provides storage for travelers transferring between road and lake craft.

characters.politics: Advocates a shared relief store for boat crews and farms isolated by high water.

characters.name: Freydis Styrsdottir
characters.description: Freydis is alert, reserved, and honest about tracks she cannot identify. She values a clean recovery more than an impressive shot.
characters.title: Guide of Elk Wood

occupations.description: Hunts for meat and hides while guiding small parties through the eastern forest.

characters.politics: Supports seasonal limits around calving grounds and resists noble hunting parties that ignore village agreements.

inventory_items.name: Belt Knife
inventory_items.notes: Used for field dressing, cord, food, and camp work.

inventory_items.name: Hunting Bow
inventory_items.notes: A familiar bow matched to her draw and hunting arrows.

characters.name: Hakon Geirsson
characters.description: Hakon is competitive, practical, and gentler with frightened animals than with indecisive buyers.
characters.title: Horse Breeder of Hestmark

occupations.description: Breeds compact working horses and accompanies sale herds to regional markets.

characters.politics: Opposes wartime seizure of breeding mares and argues that the jarl must compensate farms for fodder used by mounted retainers.

inventory_items.name: Pack Saddle
inventory_items.notes: Matched frames used to train and test working ponies.

characters.name: Ragnvald Bjornsson
characters.description: Ragnvald is unhurried, vigilant, and exact about sequences. He would rather delay a proud captain than release water badly, ground a loaded hull, or injure a hauling crew.
characters.title: Keeper of the Great Flash Weir

occupations.description: Supervises removable weir boards, barge passage, fish-bypass openings, tow crews, and witnessed maintenance shifts at the Great Flash Weir.

characters.politics: Supports standardized tolls and demands repair funds remain with the waterway instead of being diverted to court gifts.

characters.name: Rannveig Ulfsdottir
characters.description: Rannveig is spare with words and attentive to wind, birds, and swell. When conditions shift, her advice becomes deliberately cautious.
characters.title: Guide of the South Cliffs

occupations.description: Guides visitors between the landing, grazing ground, and exposed southern heights.

characters.politics: Wants island households to retain authority to close the cliff path during nesting and storm seasons despite pressure from visiting traders.

inventory_items.name: Wooden Skis
inventory_items.notes: A travel pair repaired before the first settled snow.

characters.name: Asmund Jorundsson
characters.description: Asmund is sociable, curious, and nearly impossible to hurry when figures do not balance. He enjoys bargaining but despises hidden measures, clipped coins, and vague accounts.
characters.title: Silver Warden of Tyrven
characters.politics: Enforce uniform weights and silver content while preventing private minting, clipping, and arbitrary debasement.

characters.name: Orm Ketilsson
characters.description: Orm is solitary during a burn and talkative afterward. He can read a clamp by smell and takes waste as a personal insult.
characters.title: Master Burner of Kolmark

occupations.description: Leads charcoal crews serving Jarnfell's forges under communal woodland agreements.

characters.politics: Supports woodland rotation rules and challenges forge owners who demand more charcoal than the forest can sustain.

characters.name: Njal Ketilsson
characters.description: Calm and approachable, Njal is a persistent mediator with a careful eye for toll books. He prefers settlements that both sides can explain to their neighbors without losing face.
characters.title: Jarl of Eirholm
characters.politics: Maintains neutral markets while regulating water tolls, bridge law, lock maintenance, and disputes between barge towns.

characters.name: Torsten Arnesson
characters.description: Blunt and impatient with ceremony, Torsten respects proven skill more than birth. He visits mines and forges often enough to know when an overseer is hiding a problem.
characters.title: Jarl of Jarnfell
characters.politics: Controls mine charters, labor obligations, and mountain passes while resisting distant interference in skilled work.

characters.name: Yrsa Hrolfsdottir
characters.description: Yrsa watches before she speaks and has little patience for boasting. Protective without being deferential, she judges courtiers by how they treat servants and sentries.
characters.title: First Housecarl of Tyrven
characters.politics: Keep the royal guard loyal to its oath and independent of court factions or private magnate interests.

inventory_items.name: Ash Spear
inventory_items.notes: Her usual watch weapon in hall and on the road.

inventory_items.name: Round Shield
inventory_items.notes: A serviceable shield marked for the royal household.

inventory_items.name: Mail Shirt
inventory_items.notes: Royal equipment issued for close protection in open conflict.

characters.name: Ragna Ketilsdottir
characters.description: Ragna speaks plainly, dislikes ceremony, and treats rank as irrelevant once proceedings begin. Her dry wit and exact memory make evasive testimony difficult.
characters.title: Lawspeaker of Tyrven
characters.politics: Protect customary law, open proceedings, and the assembly’s right to reject measures that bypass proper consent.

characters.name: Inga Halladottir
characters.description: Inga is disciplined, unsentimental, and protective of competent workers. She closes unsafe galleries despite pressure to meet quotas.
characters.title: Overseer of Malmberg Mine

occupations.description: Oversees crews and accounts at the district's largest iron working.

characters.politics: Insists that mine dues include timbering and drainage costs before the jarl claims a share of ore.

characters.name: Asta Hrolfsdottir
characters.description: Asta speaks plainly and notices tension before it becomes a fight. Her generosity is real but carefully accounted for.
characters.title: Mistress of the Raven Quay Guesthouse

occupations.description: Keeps a quay-side guesthouse used by fishers, pilots, and coastal traders.
A regular household craft or seasonal occupation recorded alongside public duties.

characters.politics: Presses the harbor reeve to spend quay dues on mooring posts and lamps before ceremonial feasts.

characters.name: Svenja Roriksdottir
characters.description: Svenja is strategic, self-possessed, and exacting about preparation. She can redesign a repair around scarce timber, but will not disguise weak material to meet a patron's deadline.
characters.title: Master Shipwright of Kaldhavn

occupations.description: Leads construction and major repair at Kaldhavn's principal shipyard and trains both plank-shapers and yard foremen.

characters.politics: Supports negotiated naval service but opposes taking merchant hulls or seasoned ship timber without public valuation and compensation.

inventory_items.name: Drawknife
inventory_items.notes: Used for pegs, handles, and curved fittings.

inventory_items.name: Shipwright Adze
inventory_items.notes: Kept sharp for shaping frames and inside planking.

characters.name: Eydis Ragnadottir
characters.description: Eydis is curious, candid, and careful with uncertainty. She asks about food, water, work, and symptoms before reaching for a remedy.
characters.title: Herbalist of Myrby

occupations.description: Trades dried plants and simple preparations while advising households on safe use.
A regular household craft or seasonal occupation recorded alongside public duties.

characters.politics: Supports rules protecting common herb grounds and publicly rejects healers who sell costly cures for illnesses they cannot treat.

characters.name: Thora Gisladottir
characters.description: Thora is composed, decisive, and scrupulous about posted rules. She prefers an unpopular clear decision to a convenient ambiguity.
characters.title: Harbor Master of Sudhavn

occupations.description: Administers berths, pilotage, dues, and channel notices at Sudhavn.

characters.politics: Balances merchant demands with fishing access and refuses to let the jarl's household reserve the safest berths indefinitely.

inventory_items.name: Balance Scale and Weights
inventory_items.notes: The checked harbor set used in disputed cargo measurements.

characters.name: Yngvar Leifsson
characters.description: Yngvar is patient, independent, and deeply alert to fire risk. He measures success by consistency, not by the largest possible burn.
characters.title: Pitch Master of Tjorvik

occupations.description: Produces and grades tar and pitch for river craft, roofs, and rope.

characters.politics: Argues for controlled pine-root harvest and opposes burning young stands simply to increase short-term pitch output.

characters.name: Leif Gudmundsson
characters.description: Charming, ambitious, and attentive to reputation, Leif prefers negotiated settlements that leave every faction invested in his success. He is generous in public and exacting with his stewards.
characters.title: Jarl of Solmark
characters.politics: Balances estate owners, town guilds, irrigation boards, and crown demands for stable grain taxes.

characters.name: Tove Arnesdottir
characters.description: Tove is observant, brisk, and difficult to flatter. She remembers who pays late but is quietly patient with travelers stranded by weather.
characters.title: Keeper of the North Gate Inn

occupations.description: Runs the inn with her siblings and holds its trading rights from the town.

characters.politics: Pays the town levy promptly and keeps two beds available for official messengers, but supports fixed public prices during winter shortages.

characters.name: Brand Ormsson
characters.description: Brand is methodical, soft-spoken, and proud of boards that season without twisting. He distrusts haste more than hardship.
characters.title: Master Sawyer of Hrimholt

occupations.description: A regular household craft or seasonal occupation recorded alongside public duties.
Leads a small seasonal crew at the sawpit and trains younger workers in safe handling.

characters.politics: Supports cutting quotas agreed by local freeholders and opposes granting a single merchant exclusive rights to the landing.

characters.name: Ylva Stensdottir
characters.description: Reserved and observant, Ylva speaks after others have committed themselves. She protects small freeholders, expects hunters to respect boundaries, and has little patience for waste disguised as prosperity.
characters.title: Jarl of Ravnskog
characters.politics: Upholds freeholder assemblies and forest-use limits while resisting unrestricted royal or merchant logging.

characters.name: Styrkar Halvardsson
characters.description: Styrkar is an analytical ruler who prepares several moves ahead, tests advice against reports and accounts, and rarely commits until he understands what each faction needs. Courteous but unsentimental, he relies on patience, concessions, and carefully timed pressure to keep Tyrven united.
characters.title: High King of Tyrven
characters.politics: Strengthen Tyrven by balancing the Great Thing, regional jarls, and coastal towns while improving defense without provoking a coalition against the crown.

inventory_items.name: Wool Cloak
inventory_items.notes: A heavy undyed traveling cloak fastened with a plain silver pin.

inventory_items.name: Iron Sword
inventory_items.notes: A well-maintained royal weapon worn for travel, assembly, and formal duty.

characters.name: Dalla Ketilsdottir
characters.description: Dalla is composed, practical, and unimpressed by rank. She believes careful maintenance is itself a form of reverence.
characters.title: Keeper of Keldra's Spring

occupations.description: Maintains the spring shrine while coordinating closely with the town's water users.

characters.politics: Treats the shrine and water system as one public trust and supports fines for workshops that foul the lower channel.

characters.name: Hallgrim Eiriksson
characters.description: Hallgrim is plain-spoken, compassionate, and skeptical of theatrical piety. Years at sea have made him careful about promises of safe weather.
characters.title: Keeper of Saeva's Tide Shrine

occupations.description: A retired boatman entrusted with the harbor shrine and its modest relief fund.

characters.politics: Uses shrine gifts first for fog bells, rescue rope, and support for households whose boats are lost, resisting demands for richer decoration.

characters.name: Olaf Torgilsson
characters.description: Olaf is patient with wood and impatient with boasts. Sound joints and well-seasoned timber earn his approval, regardless of a worker's family.
characters.title: Foreman of Stone Shipyard

occupations.description: Directs hull repair and small-ship construction for fishing and coastal trade.

characters.politics: Backs the harbor assembly when it resists royal requisition of boats without negotiated payment and replacement timber.

inventory_items.name: Spoon Auger
inventory_items.notes: Used for treenails and heavy hull joinery.

inventory_items.name: Shipwright Adze
inventory_items.notes: Balanced for frame and plank work at Steinvik.

characters.name: Hakon Hauksson
characters.description: Hakon manages the family's transport agreements and is known for patient bargaining with quarry crews and shipowners.
characters.title: Recognized kin of the Brannskar jarl
characters.politics: Protect quarry households from excessive levies while keeping the southern sea lanes open.

characters.name: Hrefna Oddsdottir
characters.description: Hrefna is reserved, kind, and exact with names. She dislikes superstition that frightens children away from the ordinary work of remembering the dead.
characters.title: Warden of Morna's Mound

occupations.description: Keeps the mound path and organizes winter recitations with the oldest households.

characters.politics: Protects burial ground from timber claims and insists remembrance meals remain household obligations rather than displays funded by forced dues.

characters.name: Vigdis Arnesdottir
characters.description: Vigdis is energetic, fair-minded, and attentive to weather without claiming to predict it. She turns every rite toward a practical question about seed, soil, or storage.
characters.title: Keeper of Veyr's First Furrow

occupations.description: Maintains the ceremonial plot as a seasonal duty coordinated with several farming districts.

characters.politics: Ensures seed for the civic plot comes from small farms as well as estates and publishes how the harvest portion is distributed.

characters.name: Alfhild Tovesdottir
characters.description: Alfhild is steady, warm, and quietly authoritative. She treats practical care, clean stores, and fair portions as more important than elaborate offerings.
characters.title: Keeper of Eldra's Hearth

occupations.description: Maintains the hearth shrine as a part-time civic duty alongside her household work.

characters.politics: Keeps the communal ovens open by an agreed rota and opposes any household claiming priority because of wealth or court service.

characters.name: Liv Torisdottir
characters.description: Liv is patient, firm, and attentive to cleanliness. She corrects old habits without insulting the people who learned them.
characters.title: Keeper of the Warm Springs

occupations.description: Maintains the basins and separates drinking, washing, and soaking water.

characters.politics: Treats clean drinking water as a common right and resists households that try to extend private channels from the shared flow.

characters.name: Ketil Ulfsson
characters.description: Ketil is cautious without being timid. He turns people back when cloud or thaw makes the pass unsafe and accepts their anger without argument.
characters.title: Keeper of the High Skar

occupations.description: Maintains the shelter and the upper route under an agreement witnessed at the local thing.

characters.politics: Argues that shelter timber and marker poles are a district obligation because merchants, herders, and royal riders all use the road.

inventory_items.name: Wooden Skis
inventory_items.notes: Kept ready for winter route inspection.

characters.name: Gunnar Aslaksson
characters.description: Gunnar is forceful, technically minded, and willing to reverse himself when the stone proves him wrong.
characters.title: Master of Blackstone Quarry

occupations.description: Directs building-stone extraction from the old basalt ridge.

characters.politics: Supports inspection of quarry faces by experienced workers and rejects output demands set without regard for fracture and weather.

characters.name: Bjarni Leifsson
characters.description: Bjarni is cheerful when machinery behaves and blunt when it does not. He explains every deduction from a grain sack before taking it.
characters.title: Miller of Ardal

occupations.description: A regular household craft or seasonal occupation recorded alongside public duties.
Operates Ardal Mill under hereditary rights limited by the district's water rules.

characters.politics: Favors public inspection of mill measures and water schedules, even when other mill owners call it interference.

inventory_items.name: Wooden Grain Measure
inventory_items.notes: Compared regularly with the public standard.

characters.name: Egil Knutsson
characters.description: Egil is exact, patient, and openly pleased by well-balanced machinery. He dislikes bargaining over measures already agreed at the thing.
characters.title: Miller of Kvernby

occupations.description: A regular household craft or seasonal occupation recorded alongside public duties.
Operates the largest grain mill outside Solvang and supervises two journeymen.

characters.politics: Favors shared maintenance of upstream banks because no mill can claim water it cannot keep within the channel.

inventory_items.name: Wooden Grain Measure
inventory_items.notes: Used for grain received and meal shares returned.

characters.name: Aud Ketilsdottir
characters.description: Aud is calm, deliberate, and fearless around an unsettled swarm. She shares practical knowledge but guards good breeding stock closely.
characters.title: Keeper of the Valley Hives

occupations.description: Maintains several household and communal skeps across the valley.
A regular household craft or seasonal occupation recorded alongside public duties.

characters.politics: Argues that meadow cutting dates should account for forage and nesting birds rather than only the largest hay owners.

characters.name: Astrid Gudmundsdottir
characters.description: Astrid is an able estate manager who treats reliable weights and water schedules as the basis of political peace.
characters.title: Recognized kin of the Solmark jarl
characters.politics: Protect irrigation turns, seed reserves, and public market measures from estate monopolies.

characters.name: Torunn Asgeirsdottir
characters.description: Torunn is intelligent, restrained, and formidable in questioning. She has a gift for finding the one undefined term on which an agreement could fail.
characters.title: Speaker at Haldren's Oathstone

occupations.description: Conducts witnessed oaths and assists the law reciter without holding a separate priestly office.

characters.politics: Insists that oaths name concrete duties, witnesses, and limits so powerful people cannot later hide behind vague language.

characters.name: Astrid Knutsdottir
characters.description: Practical and terse, Astrid inspects granaries and equipment herself. She listens closely to fishers, herders, and quartermasters, and distrusts plans that depend on favorable weather.
characters.title: Jarl of Frostgard
characters.politics: Defends frontier autonomy while accepting crown support tied to reliable winter stores, road patrols, and northern defense.

characters.name: Einar Torfinnsson
characters.description: Einar is easy company in public and a shrewd negotiator in private. He remembers favors, shipping losses, and which captains keep their word.
characters.title: Jarl of Skeldvik
characters.politics: Balances merchant captains, harbor law, port dues, and the naval obligations owed to the High King.

characters.name: Asa Torvaldsdottir
characters.description: Asa is inventive, demanding, and direct. She listens closely to how a broken tool was used before deciding how to repair it.
characters.title: Master Smith of Smidjadal

occupations.description: A regular household craft or seasonal occupation recorded alongside public duties.
Runs one of the valley's principal hearths and trains several apprentices.

characters.politics: Opposes noble monopolies on iron and argues that farms must receive plowshares and edge tools before ornamental commissions.

inventory_items.name: Smith Hammer and Tongs
inventory_items.notes: Her principal working set, kept at the Smidjadal forge.

inventory_items.name: Whetstone
inventory_items.notes: A fine stone reserved for finishing repaired edges.

characters.name: Sigrid Arnvidsdottir
characters.description: Sigrid is composed, economical with words, and relentlessly organized. She keeps several contingencies ready, knows which districts can spare grain or fodder, and refuses to conceal a shortfall behind flattering figures.
characters.title: Royal Steward of Tyrven
characters.politics: Maintain reliable household stores, witnessed accounts, fair conversion rates, and strict limits on what royal travel may requisition.

inventory_items.name: Balance Scale and Weights
inventory_items.notes: A checked household set for silver, stores, and disputed payments.

characters.name: Sigrun Eysteinsdottir
characters.description: Sigrun is quick-minded, hospitable, and hard to surprise. She hears every argument without pretending that every side is equally sound.
characters.title: Keeper of the Canal Inn

occupations.description: Keeps the busy inn serving barge crews, grain factors, and visitors to the southern market.

characters.politics: Supports toll-funded canal maintenance but keeps a public copy of the rates to discourage arbitrary charges.

characters.name: Hallveig Nilsdottir
characters.description: Hallveig is patient, wry, and attentive to small changes in water level. She makes decisions after hearing the oldest and youngest crew members alike.
characters.title: Net Leader of Sivholm

occupations.description: Leads a household fishing crew on the shallow reed-fringed lake.

characters.politics: Defends seasonal closures in reed spawning grounds and resists outside crews using finer nets than local custom permits.

inventory_items.name: Fishing Net
inventory_items.notes: A river net repaired each winter.

inventory_items.name: Iron Fishhooks
inventory_items.notes: Hooks for lines used when net fishing is closed or impractical.

characters.name: Haldor Veyrsson
characters.description: Haldor is genial at feasts and immovable in negotiation. He listens for positions several provinces can actually uphold, avoids promises that depend on unwilling households, and knows that his authority lasts only while the jarls trust his judgment.
characters.title: Speaker of the Jarls
characters.politics: Preserve provincial bargaining rights, coordinate shared obligations, and prevent the crown or any single jarl from treating consultation as obedience.

characters.name: Gudrun Eilifsdottir
characters.description: Gudrun is warm in company and exacting in business. She can calm a crowded room with a look and a lowered voice.
characters.title: Keeper of the Keel and Net

occupations.description: Operates a large harbor inn with hired cooks, stable hands, and two bookkeepers.

characters.politics: Maintains useful ties with quay elders but refuses private exemptions from harbor dues for wealthy captains.

characters.name: Runa Hauksdottir
characters.description: Decisive and technically minded, Runa gives engineers, quarry workers, and experienced farmers a direct hearing. She plans for bad harvests and blocked roads without treating caution as cowardice.
characters.title: Jarl of Brannskar
characters.politics: Allocates quarry rights, protects ashland farms, and requires towns to maintain emergency grain, road, and fire reserves.

characters.name: Hakon Ragnarsson
characters.description: Hakon is an orderly administrator with a talent for reconciling road obligations across districts that distrust one another.
characters.title: Recognized kin of the Vardalen jarl
characters.politics: Keep the central roads, bridge accounts, and Great Thing neutral between the provinces.

characters.name: Rolf Steinsson
characters.description: Rolf is dry-humored and even-tempered. He offers no false comfort about the road but makes sure travelers leave fed and informed.
characters.title: Keeper of the Pass Inn

occupations.description: Runs the inn serving ore carriers, smiths, guards, and travelers at the eastern pass.

characters.politics: Supports mine and road levies only when their accounts are read publicly at the Jarnfell thing.

characters.name: Ragnhild Ketilsdottir
characters.description: Ragnhild studies water levels, toll accounts, and witness testimony before committing herself to a public position.
characters.title: Recognized kin of the Eirholm jarl
characters.politics: Preserve free navigation while making weir and towpath accounts visible to every affected thing.

characters.name: Bjorn Stensson
characters.description: Bjorn knows the hauling seasons and prefers enforceable cutting plans to speeches about inexhaustible forest.
characters.title: Recognized kin of the Ravnskog jarl
characters.politics: Limit cutting to marked woodland and make fire control a shared cost of the timber trade.

characters.name: Torvald Skarsson
characters.description: Torvald is direct, restless, and intolerant of ceremonial delay. He earns loyalty by sharing hard travel and accepting the same discipline he imposes.
characters.title: Stallari of Tyrven
characters.politics: Maintain a disciplined permanent hird while keeping the wider levy prepared without exhausting farms and ports.

inventory_items.name: Iron Sword
inventory_items.notes: A commanders weapon kept plain, sharp, and immediately usable.

inventory_items.name: Iron Helmet
inventory_items.notes: A padded iron cap used for levy musters and field command.

inventory_items.name: Mail Shirt
inventory_items.notes: A carefully repaired shirt suitable for mounted travel and formation fighting.

characters.name: Ragna Torfinnsdottir
characters.description: Ragna has a navigator's caution and judges policy by whether crews can still return safely in poor weather.
characters.title: Recognized kin of the Skeldvik jarl
characters.politics: Maintain pilotage, rescue stores, and ship repair before expanding harbor dues.

commercial_ventures.name: South Road Carters’ Partnership
commercial_ventures.description: A carting partnership based at Solvang’s Southern Market. Wagons travel in numbered trains and divide loads at Kvernby and Sundby.

memberships.contribution: Regular flour cargo, loading labor, sacks, and storage beside the Great Mill.
Stable space, meals, account keeping, and the Solvang departure yard.
Twelve trained draft horses, remounts, breeding knowledge, and winter fodder contracts.
Market orders, return cargo, bridge-side lodging, and settlement of drivers’ accounts.

trade_routes.description: Carries flour, orchard goods, peat, and herbs when causeway axle limits permit.
Runs numbered wagon trains between Solvang, Kvernby, Sundby, and Vardborg.

commercial_ventures.purpose: Maintain draft teams and wagons for grain, flour, orchard goods, and return cargo on the southern roads.
commercial_ventures.capital_basis: Twelve heavy wagons, thirty-six draft horses, spare wheels and harness, fodder contracts, and working silver.

commercial_ventures.name: West Sea Shipshare
commercial_ventures.description: A shipshare based at Kaldhavn’s Inner Harbor. The ship carries salt, timber, ironwork, grain, and contracted consignments along the western sea lane.

memberships.contribution: Cargo contracts, loading crews, warehousing, and estuary pilotage at Sudhavn.
Kaldhavn provisioning, berth arrangements, cargo books, and sale of return consignments.
Spar timber, caulking labor, and repair berths at Stone Shipyard.
The principal hull share, yearly maintenance labor, and first call on the Kaldhavn yard.

trade_routes.description: Operates a scheduled coastal and river voyage from Bloomtide through Harvestwane.

commercial_ventures.purpose: Own and operate one broad-bellied coastal cargo ship between Kaldhavn, Sudhavn, Vardborg, and Eirsund.
commercial_ventures.capital_basis: A cargo hull of about sixty tonnes burden, mast and sail, anchor gear, a shipyard maintenance reserve, and voyage silver.

commercial_ventures.name: Keldu Stone Partnership
commercial_ventures.description: A working stone partnership with a yard beside Keldu Harbor. Blocks are sorted by size before loading, and damaged stone is sold locally for walls and roadwork.

memberships.contribution: Working silver, contracts taken at Eldskar, and lodging for visiting cutters.
Stone-cutting crews, quarry tools, and measured basalt from Blackstone Quarry.
Freight charters, harbor handling, and access to buyers at Sudhavn.
Recognized yard ground, road access, and arbitration of quarry boundaries.

trade_routes.description: Delivers measured basalt at Keldu Harbor under freight contracts settled before loading.

commercial_ventures.purpose: Dress Brannskar basalt to agreed measures and charter coastal carriage from Keldu Harbor to Sudhavn.
commercial_ventures.capital_basis: Quarry access, wedges and hammers, a stone yard at the harbor, loading tackle, and a shared freight fund.

commercial_ventures.name: Raven Quay Partnership
commercial_ventures.description: A seasonal boat partnership based at Raven Quay. The vessel carries dried fish, wool, lamp oil, passengers, and small consignments whenever weather permits.

memberships.contribution: Coastal pilotage, cliff-weather knowledge, and service as mate during the open season.
Working silver, Kaldhavn market contacts, and winter storage at the Keel and Net.
Nets, lines, two experienced crew, and access to the Sivholm fishery.
Guesthouse stores, victualing, account keeping, and secure space beside the quay.

trade_routes.description: Supplies preserved provisions and pilotage to larger vessels departing Raven Quay.
Carries fish, wool, passengers, and small consignments between the three partnership ports.

commercial_ventures.purpose: Fit out and operate one decked fishing and freight boat between Hrafnsfjord, Fjalloy, and Kaldhavn.
commercial_ventures.capital_basis: One clinker-built hull, sail and rigging, fishing gear, preserved provisions, and working silver for harbor dues.

commercial_ventures.name: Iron Pass Venture
commercial_ventures.description: A seasonal pass venture joining mine, forge, charcoal, and staging interests. Trains leave after the high road clears and stop before Frostfall snow closes the upper grades.

memberships.contribution: The Pass Inn yard, guarded storage, replacement animals, and meals for drivers.
Charcoal deliveries, pack animals, and fuel advances to the pass forges.
Measured ore lots, mine-side loading labor, and advances to seasonal miners.
Finished iron, wagon fittings, repair work, and inspection of purchased bars.

trade_routes.description: Operates guarded ore and iron trains during the open high-road season.
Sells iron fittings and return-load metal at the eastern end of the Ashen Road.

commercial_ventures.purpose: Purchase measured ore and ironwork, assemble guarded wagon trains, and carry them through the Iron Pass.
commercial_ventures.capital_basis: Ore-purchase silver, six reinforced wagons, draft oxen, charcoal advances, spare ironwork, and a guarded store at the pass inn.

creatures.name: Salmon
creatures.description: A migratory fish that returns from the sea to gravel rivers. Runs support nets, traps, weirs, smoking, salting, and inland trade.
creatures.habitat: Cold rivers, estuaries, and coastal feeding grounds
creatures.diet: Aquatic insects and small crustaceans when young; fish, squid, and marine invertebrates at sea.
creatures.ecological_role: Migratory fish carrying marine nutrients into rivers and feeding people, bears, otters, birds, and scavengers.
creatures.economic_uses: Fresh, smoked, dried, or salted food and a major seasonal trade catch.
creatures.seasonal_pattern: Adults ascend during established runs. Flash-weir bays and bypass channels are opened on scheduled days so breeding fish can pass upstream.

creatures.name: Herring
creatures.description: A schooling marine fish taken in seasonal abundance and preserved by salting or smoking. Failed shoals are felt quickly in coastal markets.
creatures.habitat: Coastal shelf, sounds, fjords, and sheltered bays
creatures.diet: Plankton, copepods, small crustaceans, fish larvae, and suspended organic matter.
creatures.ecological_role: Schooling forage fish supporting cod, seals, seabirds, and coastal communities.
creatures.economic_uses: Fresh, smoked, dried, or salted food; oil, bait, and fertilizer from processing remains.
creatures.seasonal_pattern: Seasonal schools approach known coasts and sounds; failed runs sharply reduce winter stores and trade.

creatures.name: Grey Seal
creatures.description: A large coastal seal that hauls out on isolated shores and follows fish into bays and fjords. Breeding sites are easily disturbed.
creatures.habitat: Rocky islands, headlands, skerries, and cold coastal water
creatures.diet: Cod, herring, flatfish, sand eels, squid, and other available marine prey.
creatures.ecological_role: Coastal marine predator influencing fish schools and transferring nutrients onto breeding shores.
creatures.economic_uses: Oil, hide, and meat under restricted local harvest; colonies also indicate productive fishing water.
creatures.seasonal_pattern: Adults gather at established breeding shores, then disperse to feeding grounds; storms and shore ice change haul-out use.

creatures.name: Northern Pike
creatures.description: A large freshwater ambush fish important to lake and wetland communities, especially where winter access to the coast is poor.
creatures.habitat: Vegetated lakes, slow rivers, backwaters, and marsh channels
creatures.diet: Fish, amphibians, aquatic insects, and occasional waterbirds or small mammals.
creatures.ecological_role: Ambush predator regulating lake and slow-river fish communities.
creatures.economic_uses: Fresh, dried, or smoked food, especially where winter netting is practical.
creatures.seasonal_pattern: Pike move into shallow flooded margins to spawn after ice-out and return to weed beds and deeper water afterward.

creatures.name: Wolverine
creatures.description: A wide-ranging scavenger and hunter of cold country, powerful for its size and capable of opening frozen carcasses.
creatures.habitat: Northern mountain, tundra, snowfield margin, and high forest
creatures.diet: Carrion, reindeer calves, hare, rodents, birds, eggs, and prey cached under snow or rock.
creatures.ecological_role: Wide-ranging northern scavenger and predator that redistributes carrion through harsh uplands.
creatures.economic_uses: Dense fur and limited control where repeated losses occur at traps or food caches.
creatures.seasonal_pattern: Wolverines range widely in winter, cache food, and use secluded snow dens for young.

creatures.name: Eurasian Lynx
creatures.description: A solitary ambush hunter of hare and deer. It moves quietly through large territories and is seldom seen near busy settlements.
creatures.habitat: Dense forest, rocky woodland, and broken upland cover
creatures.diet: Mountain hare, roe-sized deer where present, young reindeer, birds, and occasional small livestock.
creatures.ecological_role: Solitary woodland predator regulating hare and small-ungulate populations.
creatures.economic_uses: Winter fur and targeted control after repeated losses near settlements.
creatures.seasonal_pattern: Ranges widen in winter; females den in secluded rocky or wooded cover and raise kittens through summer.

creatures.name: Otter
creatures.description: An aquatic hunter of fish, crustaceans, and amphibians. Tracks and slides are more often found than the animal itself.
creatures.habitat: Clean rivers, lakes, estuaries, and sheltered rocky coast
creatures.diet: Fish, crayfish, frogs, aquatic insects, mollusks, and occasional waterbirds.
creatures.ecological_role: Semi-aquatic predator indicating connected, productive rivers, lakes, and sheltered coasts.
creatures.economic_uses: Fur under restricted trapping and observation of fish movement; excessive harvest is discouraged near breeding holts.
creatures.seasonal_pattern: Otters remain active year-round, shifting between open channels, coasts, and ice-free springs as water freezes.

creatures.name: European Eel
creatures.description: A long-bodied migratory fish of connected lowland waters. Eels move through wet grass and shallow channels during damp nights and gather at managed passages.
creatures.habitat: Slow rivers, connected lakes, marsh channels, and estuaries
creatures.diet: Aquatic insects, worms, crustaceans, mollusks, carrion, and small fish.
creatures.ecological_role: Migratory nocturnal predator connecting inland food webs with the sea.
creatures.economic_uses: Taken in traps and weirs, then eaten fresh, smoked, or salted.
creatures.seasonal_pattern: Adults descend toward the sea in autumn; managed bypass channels remain open during peak downstream movement.

creatures.name: Beaver
creatures.description: A large aquatic rodent that fells small trees and builds lodges and dams, creating ponds that alter drainage, fish habitat, and hay ground.
creatures.habitat: Slow rivers, lake outlets, wooded banks, and sheltered wetlands
creatures.diet: Willow, birch, aspen, aquatic plants, bark, twigs, and stored woody cuttings.
creatures.ecological_role: Wetland engineer whose dams retain water, trap sediment, and create ponds used by fish, birds, and grazing animals.
creatures.economic_uses: Hide, meat, castoreum, and occasional managed water control; dam removal is regulated where roads or fields are threatened.
creatures.seasonal_pattern: Pairs repair dams through the open-water season and store branches before freeze-up; winter activity continues beneath the ice.

creatures.name: Grey Cod
creatures.description: A bottom-feeding marine fish caught by handline and longline. Drying makes it a dependable cargo for inland districts.
creatures.habitat: Cool coastal banks, rocky seabed, and deeper fjords
creatures.diet: Small fish, crustaceans, worms, mollusks, and benthic invertebrates.
creatures.ecological_role: Demersal marine predator and prey supporting seals, larger fish, seabirds, and coastal fisheries.
creatures.economic_uses: Fresh, dried, or salted food; liver oil and offal support household uses.
creatures.seasonal_pattern: Inshore availability shifts with spawning, water temperature, and storms; drying is concentrated in cold windy months.

creatures.name: Wild Boar
creatures.description: A powerful omnivore that roots for mast, tubers, worms, and carrion. It damages crops and is most dangerous when wounded or defending young.
creatures.habitat: Southern broadleaf forest, marsh edge, and fields near woodland
creatures.diet: Acorns, roots, tubers, fungi, grain, fruit, insects, eggs, carrion, and small animals.
creatures.ecological_role: Powerful omnivorous forager disturbing soil, dispersing seed, and competing with woodland pigs and farms.
creatures.economic_uses: Meat, hide, tusk, bristles, and crop-protection hunting.
creatures.seasonal_pattern: Boar range follows mast and crops; winter groups use sheltered woodland while adult males remain more solitary.

creatures.name: Red Deer
creatures.description: A large grazing and browsing deer of mixed country. Stags are dangerous at close range during the autumn rut.
creatures.habitat: Southern and western woodland, forest edge, heath, and open grazing ground
creatures.diet: Grass, herbs, leaves, shoots, acorns, bark, and winter browse.
creatures.ecological_role: Large grazer-browser shaping woodland edges and supporting wolves, lynx, scavengers, and hunters.
creatures.economic_uses: Meat, hide, sinew, antler, bone, and ceremonial or household craft material.
creatures.seasonal_pattern: Herds move between summer uplands and sheltered winter valleys; the autumn rut concentrates adults.

creatures.name: Forest Pig
creatures.description: A long-legged domestic pig driven into woodland for mast and brought close to the farm before winter slaughter. It is valued for meat and fat.
creatures.habitat: Farmyards, stubble, and broadleaf woodland near settled districts
creatures.diet: Mast, roots, tubers, fungi, household waste, insects, and occasional carrion.
creatures.ecological_role: Domestic woodland forager converting seasonal mast and scraps into meat, fat, bristles, and manure.
creatures.economic_uses: Pork, lard, hide, bristles, manure, and waste consumption.
creatures.seasonal_pattern: Herds forage in woodland after mast fall and most surplus animals are slaughtered before winter feed becomes scarce.

creatures.name: Tyrven Short-tail Sheep
creatures.description: A hardy sheep with a short tail and weather-resistant fleece. It supplies wool, meat, skins, and some milk on ground too poor for grain.
creatures.habitat: Coastal grass, upland pasture, heath, and dry farm margins
creatures.diet: Grass, herbs, heather, sedges, hay, and dried leaf fodder.
creatures.ecological_role: Domestic grazer converting marginal pasture into wool, milk, meat, hide, and manure.
creatures.economic_uses: Wool, cloth, milk, cheese, meat, hide, horn, manure, and portable household wealth.
creatures.seasonal_pattern: Flocks move to summer grazing, are shorn before warm weather, breed in autumn, and return to sheltered winter ground.

creatures.name: Northern Pony
creatures.description: A small, strong horse used for riding, packs, carts, timber haulage, and light fieldwork. Its winter ration limits ownership more than pasture does.
creatures.habitat: Farm roads, forest tracks, upland pasture, and settled valleys
creatures.diet: Grass, sedges, herbs, hay, straw, and limited leaf fodder.
creatures.ecological_role: Domestic grazer and transport animal adapted to small loads, rough roads, snow, and sparse forage.
creatures.economic_uses: Riding, pack work, light cartage, manure, hair, hide, and emergency meat.
creatures.seasonal_pattern: Ponies graze common land through summer; working and breeding animals receive hay while surplus stock is sold or slaughtered before winter.

creatures.name: Brown Bear
creatures.description: A solitary omnivore that ranges widely for plants, insects, fish, and carrion before winter denning. Most avoid settlements unless food is left exposed.
creatures.habitat: Remote forest, berry ground, mountain woodland, and quiet caves
creatures.diet: Roots, berries, mast, insects, fish, carrion, and occasional young ungulates or livestock.
creatures.ecological_role: Large omnivore, scavenger, seed carrier, and intermittent predator at the edge of settled land.
creatures.economic_uses: Hide, fat, meat, and protection bounties where repeated livestock losses occur.
creatures.seasonal_pattern: Bears feed heavily before winter denning; females emerge later with cubs and avoid busy settlements when possible.

creatures.name: Grey Wolf
creatures.description: A pack hunter of deer and other ungulates. Wolves usually avoid people but take poorly guarded stock during hard winters.
creatures.habitat: Large forests, northern valleys, tundra margins, and sparsely settled uplands
creatures.diet: Deer, reindeer, moose calves, hare, carrion, and poorly guarded livestock.
creatures.ecological_role: Pack predator shaping wild-herd movement and removing vulnerable animals and carrion.
creatures.economic_uses: Fur and targeted control near livestock districts; broad eradication is avoided where wild herds depend on predation.
creatures.seasonal_pattern: Packs follow wintering herds, den in spring, and range more widely when snow or prey conditions deteriorate.

creatures.name: Rock Ptarmigan
creatures.description: A ground bird of open cold country whose seasonal plumage follows the snow. It is taken for winter meat but remains vulnerable near nesting ground.
creatures.habitat: Northern plateau, mountain heath, scree, and snowfield margin
creatures.diet: Willow and birch buds, leaves, berries, seeds, flowers, and insects taken chiefly by chicks.
creatures.ecological_role: Tundra herbivore and prey for raptors, foxes, lynx, and northern hunters.
creatures.economic_uses: Seasonal meat and feathers under local hunting limits.
creatures.seasonal_pattern: Plumage follows the snow season; birds form winter flocks and separate into breeding territories after thaw.

creatures.name: Common Eider
creatures.description: A sea duck that nests in coastal colonies and feeds on mussels and other shallow-water animals. Down is gathered after nests are left.
creatures.habitat: Low islands, sheltered rocky coasts, and skerries
creatures.diet: Mussels, clams, snails, small crustaceans, sea urchins, and other shallow-water invertebrates.
creatures.ecological_role: Coastal benthic feeder linking shellfish beds with marine predators and nesting-island nutrient cycles.
creatures.economic_uses: Down gathered from managed nests after lining is replaced, with limited eggs and birds taken under island custom.
creatures.seasonal_pattern: Colonies gather on sheltered islands in spring; females nest close together and flocks move to open feeding water after breeding.

creatures.name: Moose
creatures.description: The largest forest browser in Tyrven. It feeds on shoots, aquatic plants, and young trees and is hunted cautiously for meat and hide.
creatures.habitat: Boreal forest, willow scrub, lake margins, and wet ground
creatures.diet: Willow, birch, rowan, aquatic plants, sedges, bark, and young shoots.
creatures.ecological_role: Large browser opening dense regrowth and providing prey and carrion for large predators.
creatures.economic_uses: Meat, hide, sinew, antler, bone, and limited protection of crops and hay stores.
creatures.seasonal_pattern: Moose use wetlands in summer, browse woody valleys in winter, calve in secluded cover, and gather loosely during the rut.

creatures.name: Yard Hen
creatures.description: A small landrace fowl kept for eggs, meat, feathers, and the use of household scraps. Most birds are housed closely in severe winter weather.
creatures.habitat: Farmyards and sheltered village plots
creatures.diet: Grain, seeds, insects, worms, kitchen scraps, and forage gathered around yards and dung heaps.
creatures.ecological_role: Domestic omnivore converting household scraps and invertebrates into eggs, meat, feathers, and manure.
creatures.economic_uses: Eggs, meat, feathers, manure, and pest reduction around stored fodder and farmyards.
creatures.seasonal_pattern: Laying rises with spring light and forage; households retain breeding birds and slaughter surplus young before winter.

creatures.name: Capercaillie
creatures.description: A very large forest grouse. Males defend display grounds in spring, while hens nest on the ground under cover.
creatures.habitat: Mature conifer forest, bog edge, and quiet woodland clearings
creatures.diet: Pine needles, buds, berries, shoots, seeds, and insects taken especially by growing chicks.
creatures.ecological_role: Large forest grouse that consumes woodland plants and supports lynx, foxes, raptors, and human hunters.
creatures.economic_uses: Seasonal meat and feathers under local woodland hunting rules.
creatures.seasonal_pattern: Males gather at spring display grounds; broods feed on insects in summer and adults rely more heavily on conifer browse in winter.

creatures.name: Farm Dog
creatures.description: A medium working dog used to guard yards, move stock, track wounded game, and warn isolated households.
creatures.habitat: Farmsteads, pasture, fishing camps, halls, and road stations
creatures.diet: Household scraps, offal, porridge, dairy waste, fish remnants, and small prey caught around farms.
creatures.ecological_role: Domestic guard, herding aid, vermin hunter, tracker, and companion within settled landscapes.
creatures.economic_uses: Herding, guarding, hunting, tracking, alarm, warmth, and companionship.
creatures.seasonal_pattern: Dogs work year-round; breeding and training are timed so young animals mature before demanding winter or summer work.

creatures.name: Crag Goat
creatures.description: A sure-footed browsing animal kept in small herds for milk, meat, hide, and horn. Close herding protects young trees and winter browse.
creatures.habitat: Rocky slopes, scrub woodland, island pasture, and marginal farm ground
creatures.diet: Coarse grass, sedges, dwarf shrubs, browse, hay, and dried leaf fodder.
creatures.ecological_role: Domestic browser converting steep and scrubby ground into milk, meat, hide, horn, manure, and limited pack work.
creatures.economic_uses: Milk, cheese, meat, hide, horn, hair, manure, and light loads.
creatures.seasonal_pattern: Herds climb to summer grazing and return before deep snow; breeding females receive the best stored browse and hay.

creatures.name: Mountain Hare
creatures.description: A common northern hare whose coat lightens in winter. It feeds many predators and is trapped or hunted for meat and fur.
creatures.habitat: Heath, tundra, scrub, pasture edge, and open forest
creatures.diet: Grass, herbs, heather, buds, bark, and twigs, with woody browse dominating under snow.
creatures.ecological_role: Small herbivore and major prey for lynx, wolves, raptors, and human hunters.
creatures.economic_uses: Meat and winter fur taken with snares under local seasonal rules.
creatures.seasonal_pattern: Coat color and range shift with snow cover; repeated litters are possible during the growing season.

creatures.name: Brown Honeybee
creatures.description: A dark, cold-tolerant honeybee managed in straw or wooden skeps for honey, wax, and orchard pollination.
creatures.habitat: Orchards, meadows, woodland edges, and sheltered apiaries
creatures.diet: Nectar, pollen, stored honey, and water collected within the hive's forage range.
creatures.ecological_role: Managed pollinator of orchards, hay meadows, gardens, and woodland-edge plants.
creatures.economic_uses: Honey, wax, orchard pollination, and small traded colonies.
creatures.seasonal_pattern: Colonies expand in spring, swarm in early summer, store through bloom, and cluster around reserves during winter.

creatures.name: Reindeer
creatures.description: A migratory northern deer that follows exposed winter grazing and greener summer valleys. Ice over pasture can cause sudden losses.
creatures.habitat: Northern tundra, windswept plateau, open valley, and seasonal snow ground
creatures.diet: Lichens, sedges, grasses, herbs, dwarf shrubs, fungi, and woody browse.
creatures.ecological_role: Cold-country grazer linking tundra plants with wolves, wolverines, scavengers, and northern hunters.
creatures.economic_uses: Meat, hide, sinew, antler, bone, and seasonal exchange with northern households.
creatures.seasonal_pattern: Herds move between calving, summer insect relief, autumn rutting, and wind-scoured winter feeding grounds.

creatures.name: Tyrven Cattle
creatures.description: A compact landrace kept for milk, draft work, meat, hide, horn, and manure. Herds remain small where hay and leaf fodder are scarce.
creatures.habitat: Sheltered farmsteads, river valleys, and southern plains
creatures.diet: Grass, hay, straw, sedges, leaf fodder, crop residues, and limited grain by-products.
creatures.ecological_role: Domestic grazer and draft animal converting meadow and crop residues into milk, meat, traction, hide, horn, and manure.
creatures.economic_uses: Milk, butter, cheese, meat, draft work, hide, horn, bone, manure, and household wealth.
creatures.seasonal_pattern: Cattle graze through summer; breeding cows and draft oxen receive priority in winter while surplus animals are slaughtered after harvest.

creatures.name: Grey Goose
creatures.description: A domestic goose kept for meat, fat, eggs, feathers, and watchfulness around the yard. Flocks graze wet grass and harvested fields.
creatures.habitat: Wet meadows, farm ponds, stubble, and river settlements
creatures.diet: Grass, grain, sedges, aquatic plants, vegetable scraps, and small invertebrates taken while grazing.
creatures.ecological_role: Domestic grazer and alarm bird around farmyards, wet meadows, and stubble fields.
creatures.economic_uses: Meat, fat, eggs, feathers, down, manure, and household alarm.
creatures.seasonal_pattern: Birds graze through the open season; most young are fattened on aftermath and stubble before autumn slaughter.

galaxies.name: Elvstjerne
galaxies.description: Elvstjerne is a barred spiral galaxy. From Audrun, its disk appears as a pale, irregular band across the night sky, broken by dark lanes of interstellar dust.

assemblies.name: Ravnskog Provincial Thing
assemblies.description: The provincial assembly is held at the principal thing ground of Ravnskog.
assemblies.meeting_cycle: Meets at the opening of summer and after harvest, with emergency sessions called for invasion, famine, flood, or a disputed succession.
assemblies.membership_rule: Each hold sends customary delegates chosen at its local thing. Free householders may attend, while litigants, witnesses, law-panel members, the jarl, and the jarl's steward have formal duties.
assemblies.jurisdiction: Confirms the provincial jarl, hears appeals from local things, coordinates roads and defense, apportions provincial dues, and settles disputes crossing hold boundaries.
assemblies.appeal_path: Unresolved disputes involving common law, another province, or misconduct by the jarl may be carried to the Great Thing.
assemblies.enforcement: Sureties and local officers execute judgments. The jarl supplies force only after a witnessed order or an immediate breach of the peace.

assemblies.name: Langaker Local Thing
assemblies.description: An open assembly ground on firm, accessible land in Langaker. Free householders gather here to hear law, settle disputes, witness agreements, and organize common obligations.
assemblies.meeting_cycle: Meets at least twice yearly and when urgent disputes, inheritance, boundary work, or communal maintenance require witnesses.
assemblies.membership_rule: Free householders may attend. Established households select law-panel members and delegates according to local custom; dependents may appear as litigants or witnesses through recognized advocates.
assemblies.jurisdiction: Hears ordinary disputes, witnesses transfers and inheritances, organizes common labor, selects local officers, and records delegates for the provincial thing.
assemblies.appeal_path: A party may appeal a disputed judgment to the provincial thing after providing surety for attendance and costs.
assemblies.enforcement: Named sureties, compensation schedules, distraint, temporary exclusion from common resources, and provincial assistance support enforcement.

assemblies.name: Great Thing of Tyrven
assemblies.description: Tyrven's common assembly occupies the Vardalen thing ground near the central roads, where pasture, water, fuel, booths, and guarded storage support a large seasonal gathering.
assemblies.meeting_cycle: The principal assembly meets once each summer; extraordinary sessions require the lawspeaker and at least five provincial delegations.
assemblies.membership_rule: Free householders may attend and speak through local delegations. Jarls, appointed law-panel members, recognized litigants, witnesses, and petitioners have defined places in the proceedings.
assemblies.jurisdiction: Confirms the High King and lawspeaker, enacts common law, hears disputes between provinces, reviews extraordinary levies, and grants exemptions from common rules.
assemblies.appeal_path: Local judgments pass to the provincial thing. Matters between provinces, disputed provincial judgments, and questions of common law may reach the Great Thing.
assemblies.enforcement: Judgments are enforced by named sureties, property seizure, compensation, outlawry, and the coordinated authority of the provinces; the lawspeaker commands no private army.

timelines.name: Tyrven Annals

events.name: Southern Brine Rights
events.description: Solmark granted shoreline, coppice, peat, pan-repair, and packing rights to the brine houses above the gulf, securing an internal supply of preserving salt.

events.name: Deep Gallery Charter
events.description: Jarnfell required chartered mines to maintain drainage, timber inventories, crew tallies, road shares, and compensation funds before opening deeper galleries.

events.name: Present Reckoning
events.description: The current political offices, economic estimates, tax assessments, routes, and public works are recorded in year 418 of the Age of the Nine Provinces.

events.name: Provincial Succession Settlement
events.description: The Great Thing standardized the hearing of jarldom claims while preserving provincial choice. Recognition by the crown became a record of settlement, not a power to appoint without assent.

events.name: Thin Harvest of 403
events.description: A continent-wide poor harvest triggered reserve releases, reduced brewing, controlled livestock slaughter, and temporary suspension of several dues without exhausting the revised grain stores.

events.name: Three-Winter Scarcity
events.description: Three poor northern harvests reduced herds and emptied several household stores. Provincial relief began with remitted dues, controlled slaughter, and grain purchased from the south.

events.name: Western Harbor Compact
events.description: Kaldhavn and Vesthavn standardized pilotage, rescue stores, harbor measures, and the public revenue shares used for beacons and breakwaters.

events.name: Kaldhavn Harbor Foundation
events.description: Skeldvik households consolidated older landing places into a guarded inner harbor with pilotage turns, repair yards, rescue stores, and public quay measures.

events.name: Common Weights Register
events.description: Market and toll stations received checked copies of standard weights and witnessed value bands. Offices were required to separate public receipts from household income.

events.name: Reserve Granary Law
events.description: After a thin harvest, the provinces adopted witnessed reserve targets, storage-loss allowances, rotation of old grain, and rules for opening public stores.

events.name: Open-Lineage Judgment
events.description: The Great Thing confirmed that a recognized adult of a ruling lineage could present a claim through either parent. Provincial assent, household leadership, and sureties remained decisive.

events.name: Termed Service Law
events.description: The Great Thing limited hereditary bondage, established witnessed terms for debt service, and required a lawful path to redemption. Unfree service continued but could no longer pass indefinitely without review.

events.name: Election of Styrkar
events.description: The Great Thing chose Styrkar after he assembled a workable coalition on road maintenance, reserve inspection, and limits on provincial military rivalry.

events.name: Great Eirwater Flood
events.description: Spring flood carried away bridges and fish weirs across Eirholm. Rebuilding established witnessed toll accounts, fish-bypass days, and common hauling duties.

events.name: Opening of the Iron Pass
events.description: Jarnfell and Vardalen completed the marked high road, shelters, load measures, and customary maintenance shares that made regular iron cartage possible.

events.name: Frostgard Grazing Compact
events.description: Northern holds recorded summer grazing bounds, autumn slaughter dates, hay obligations, and emergency access to sheltered browse after repeated winter disputes.

events.name: Reckoning Reform
events.description: The lawspeaker fixed seven feast days after the final winter month every seventh year, aligning court seasons and household accounts with the observed solar year.

events.name: Compact of Nine Provinces
events.description: Delegates joined an older network of local things to an elective crown. Nine provincial jarls retained regional authority while the lawspeaker and Great Thing received control of common law.

events.name: First Crown Settlement
events.description: The first vacancy proved that the crown was not hereditary. Provincial delegations rejected two close heirs and selected a compromise candidate after sureties were exchanged.

events.name: Gronvale Fair Charter
events.description: Frostgard and Vardalen fixed safe-conduct days, pasture limits, and public measures for the autumn horse and wool fair at Gronvale.

events.name: Wolf Winter
events.description: Deep snow concentrated deer and livestock in the valleys. Coordinated watches protected herds while the things restricted wasteful den hunting and divided compensation claims.

timelines.description: A working chronology used by assemblies, households, and later compilers to place settlements, laws, disasters, and public works.

eras.name: Age of the Nine Provinces
eras.description: The era begins with the compact that fixed the duties of the Great Thing, the provincial jarls, and the elective crown.

lore_connections.name: Morna's Mound Shrine devotion
lore_connections.description: Ravnby households honor Morna through accurate names, maintained turf, and winter remembrance meals.

lore_connections.name: Saeva's Tide Shrine devotion
lore_connections.description: Kaldhavn's coastal households maintain Saeva's rites alongside rescue equipment and missing-boat records.

lore_connections.name: Shipyard Timber Contract
lore_connections.description: Sten supplies boards and selected curved timber through the marked forest trade; Svenja rejects hidden rot and pays more for properly seasoned stock.

lore_connections.name: Keldra's Spring Shrine devotion
lore_connections.description: Eldskar households connect Keldra with clean shared water, useful stone, and materials taken without waste.

lore_connections.name: Lawspeaker and District Lawman
lore_connections.description: Ragna recognized Solveig's precision and supports her authority to challenge vague settlements at Eikvang.

lore_connections.name: Skarven's Road Cairn devotion
lore_connections.description: Travelers honor Skarven by repairing the cairn, clearing the track, and preserving honest boundary marks.

lore_connections.name: Brannskar Quarry Compact
lore_connections.description: Runa protects technical closures and quarry inspection, while Gunnar accepts public stone duties only when extraction costs and dangerous faces are honestly recorded.

lore_connections.name: Forest Counsel
lore_connections.description: Freydis reports calving grounds, hunting pressure, and illegal noble parties; Ylva turns those observations into limits the local things can enforce.

lore_connections.name: Law and Oath Practice
lore_connections.description: They coordinate the legal wording of public oaths so ritual form cannot conceal an undefined duty.

lore_connections.name: Haldren's Oath Shrine devotion
lore_connections.description: Vardborg traders invoke Haldren when disputed measures or bargains require witnesses.

lore_connections.name: King and Steward
lore_connections.description: Styrkar relies on Sigrid for unsentimental accounts and feasible travel plans. She supports his strategy but refuses to make shortages disappear on paper.

lore_connections.name: Mother and Daughter at the Hearth
lore_connections.description: Alfhild is Tove's adult daughter. They share household obligations but disagree amicably over how much inn food should be committed to communal winter relief.

lore_connections.name: South Headland Shrine devotion
lore_connections.description: Fjalloy families keep a hooded lamp for Saeva during exposed autumn crossings.

lore_connections.name: Two Shipyards, One Standard
lore_connections.description: Svenja trained Olaf in hull layout before he took charge at Steinvik. He now challenges her judgments when smaller boats require different compromises.

lore_connections.name: Saeva's Quay Shrine devotion
lore_connections.description: Boat crews honor Saeva before departure and report hazards when they return.

lore_connections.name: Eldra's Hearth Shrine devotion
lore_connections.description: Households honor Eldra here through shared ovens, fair portions, and winter-store obligations.

lore_connections.name: Crown and Law
lore_connections.description: They agree that Tyrven requires a strong common law, but Ragna publicly limits royal improvisation and Styrkar tests how far necessity can stretch accepted custom.

lore_connections.name: Morna's Ancestor Cairn devotion
lore_connections.description: Elgmark families connect Morna with dignified burial ground and the clearing of paths before winter rites.

lore_connections.name: Keldra's Forge Shrine devotion
lore_connections.description: Miners and smiths honor Keldra through careful material use and the remelting of workable scrap.

lore_connections.name: Skarven's Crossing Shrine devotion
lore_connections.description: Barge crews connect Skarven with fair passage, visible tolls, and reliable warnings.

lore_connections.name: Veyr's Meadow Shrine devotion
lore_connections.description: The meadow rite joins hay timing, nesting protection, and winter fodder for weak animals.

lore_connections.name: Crown and Provincial Council
lore_connections.description: Their rivalry concerns authority rather than personal hatred. Styrkar seeks coordinated action; Haldor insists that promises must survive scrutiny by jarls and local things.

lore_connections.name: Mine Safety and Revenue
lore_connections.description: They depend on each other but dispute the acceptable cost of delay. Inga closes unsafe galleries; Torsten must answer for lost revenue and defense supply.

lore_connections.name: Harbor and Waterway Rules
lore_connections.description: They compare toll tallies, draft limits, and hazard reports so sea and inland carriers cannot exploit contradictory rules at either end of the route.

lore_connections.name: Eldra's Reed Shrine devotion
lore_connections.description: Flood-isolated households honor Eldra through food relief, clean mats, and practical care.

lore_connections.name: Frostgard Pass Mandate
lore_connections.description: Astrid protects Ketil's authority to close the High Skar against merchants who would risk lives to preserve a schedule.

lore_connections.name: Ore to Hearth
lore_connections.description: Inga supplies honestly graded ore and blooms; Asa reports brittle or contaminated batches rather than quietly passing failed material into cheaper tools.

lore_connections.name: Shrine Below Stone devotion
lore_connections.description: Mine crews honor Keldra at the surface tally rather than carrying an open flame into unsafe workings.

lore_connections.name: Myrholt Flood Compact
lore_connections.description: Svala backs Finn's labor calls when high water crosses hold boundaries, while he keeps enough detail for her accounts to be challenged at the thing.

lore_connections.name: Solmark Water Account
lore_connections.description: Leif needs predictable grain movement; Egil supports shared water rules but resists any schedule written only for the largest estates.

lore_connections.name: Ravnskog Fire Compact
lore_connections.description: Ylva uses Yngvar's fire and pitch knowledge when setting woodland limits; he relies on her to enforce them against wealthy outsiders.

lore_connections.name: Kaldhavn Yard Charter
lore_connections.description: Einar grants yard rights and negotiates naval obligations; Svenja demands public valuation for seized hulls, seasoned timber, and skilled labor.

lore_connections.name: Winter Names and Living Stores
lore_connections.description: Hrefna keeps remembrance obligations accurate while Signe helps identify timber and trading households able to support bereaved families through winter.

lore_connections.name: Eirholm Passage Mandate
lore_connections.description: Njal delegates daily weir order to Ragnvald and accepts that safety may interrupt toll collection or a favored captain's schedule.

lore_connections.name: Haldren's Oathstone devotion
lore_connections.description: Witnessed public oaths at Eikvang invoke Haldren's concern with exact duties and truthful speech.

lore_connections.name: Fen Food and Remedies
lore_connections.description: Hallveig supplies fish oil, clean reeds, and preserved catch; Eydis provides safe wound washes and identifies plants that should not enter food stores.

lore_connections.name: Veyr's First Furrow devotion
lore_connections.description: Several farming districts sow seed together here so Veyr's rite cannot become one estate's possession.

lore_connections.name: Harbor Relief Partnership
lore_connections.description: Hallgrim manages rescue stores and missing-boat records; Gudrun provides rooms, food, and witnessed distribution when several households need help at once.

moons.name: Mani
moons.description: Mani is a pale, cratered moon completing its sidereal passage in 27.08 days. Its visible phase cycle lasts about 29.25 days and provides the coastal count used by fishers and navigators.
moons.tidal_role: Mani raises the principal coastal tide. Spring and neap tides govern harbor depths, weir work, coastal departures, and the strongest estuary currents.
